title: Monotonicity of Ising spectral gaps
formal:
Does strengthening any collection of ferromagnetic interactions always weakly decrease the spectral gap of zero-field random-site heat-bath Ising dynamics on a fixed finite vertex set? For every integer \(n\ge1\), put \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Let \(J=(J_{uv})_{u<v}\) and \(J'=(J'_{uv})_{u<v}\) be finite nonnegative real interaction strengths on the unordered vertex pairs. Is the following statement true?
\[\bigl[\forall u<v,\ 0\le J_{uv}\le J'_{uv}\bigr]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\gamma(J')\le\gamma(J).\]
Here \(\gamma\) is the spectral gap per individual uniformly chosen site update, defined below. There is no external magnetic field or fixed boundary spin. This is the common interaction-strength generalization explicitly asked in Question 2 of the source.
why: The conjecture asks whether stronger attractive interactions universally slow the relaxation of local sampling. A positive answer would give a comparison principle across both temperature and graph structure, while a counterexample would expose a limit of that basic physical intuition. The difficulty is a global dynamical property, even though each update uses only the neighboring spins.
status_note: The 2017 textbook question and the Nacu, Kargin and Salez primary manuscripts were read on 2026-09-14. The first two establish restricted cases; Salez studies monotonicity in the state order rather than in the couplings. A bounded later-work search through the review date found no matching arbitrary-graph resolution. This records source-open status, not an exhaustive verification of present openness.

importance.reason: A general comparison principle for the relaxation of ferromagnetic sampling, combining temperature and graph modifications. Its significance lies in a universal relation between interactions and dynamics, beyond bounds for one lattice or one parameter regime.
importance.basis: Individual review of the textbook formulation, Nacu’s cycle theorem, Kargin’s mean-field theorem and the distinct monotonicity notion in Salez’s 2023 result.

sentences: A ferromagnetic Ising model favors neighboring spins that agree.
This question asks whether increasing its interactions always reduces the spectral gap of local heat-bath updates.
The graph has a fixed vertex set, arbitrary nonnegative edge strengths and no external field.
The spectral gap is defined from the exact transition matrix and measures the relaxation rate.
The checked cycle and equal-coupling complete-graph theorems do not cover independent interaction changes on arbitrary graphs.

definitions:
The state space is \(\Omega=\{-1,+1\}^{V}\). Use the symmetric convention \(J_{vu}=J_{uv}\) and \(J_{vv}=0\). The Gibbs probability of a configuration is
\[\pi_J(\sigma)=Z_J^{-1}\exp\!\left(\sum_{u<v}J_{uv}\sigma_u\sigma_v\right),\qquad Z_J=\sum_{\tau\in\Omega}\exp\!\left(\sum_{u<v}J_{uv}\tau_u\tau_v\right).\]
Each unordered pair is counted once. A zero interaction means the corresponding edge is absent, so arbitrary finite graphs, isolated vertices and edge additions are included. Inverse temperature is absorbed into the interactions. All couplings are finite; the infinite-coupling limit is not a separate input.

At each step choose \(v\in V\) uniformly, independently of previous choices. Set \(h_v(\sigma)=\sum_{u\ne v}J_{uv}\sigma_u\). Replace the spin at \(v\) by \(+1\) with probability
\[\frac{\exp(h_v(\sigma))}{\exp(h_v(\sigma))+\exp(-h_v(\sigma))},\]
and by \(-1\) otherwise; all other spins stay fixed. Retaining the current spin counts as one update. Write \(P_J(\sigma,\tau)\) for this transition probability. The chain is finite, irreducible and reversible with stationary distribution \(\pi_J\).

For \(f:\Omega\to\mathbb R\), set \(\overline f_J=\sum_\sigma\pi_J(\sigma)f(\sigma)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_J}(f)=\sum_\sigma\pi_J(\sigma)(f(\sigma)-\overline f_J)^2\). Define
\[\gamma(J)=\inf_{\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_J}(f)>0}\frac{\frac12\sum_{\sigma,\tau\in\Omega}\pi_J(\sigma)P_J(\sigma,\tau)(f(\sigma)-f(\tau))^2}{\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_J}(f)}.\]
Equivalently, this is \(1-\lambda_2(P_J)\), with eigenvalues ordered decreasingly and the stationary eigenvalue \(1\) first. The heat-bath matrix has nonnegative eigenvalues because it averages conditional-expectation projections. Thus the spectral and absolute spectral gap agree for this update rule. The relaxation time is \(1/\gamma(J)\).

Both compared chains have exactly the same \(n\) sites and site-selection probabilities. Adding an edge does not add a vertex or rescale the clock. The assertion uses a non-strict inequality and does not assume differentiability of eigenvalues. The question is about exact real transition matrices; numerical simulation or a choice of finite-precision implementation does not define the target.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the displayed universal implication, or a Lean-checked refutation. A refutation may specify a finite vertex set and two allowed interaction arrays \(J\le J'\) and prove \(\gamma(J')>\gamma(J)\). A positive answer must cover arbitrary graph structure and independent changes in edge strengths, including edges of initial strength zero. A theorem only for common rescaling of all interactions, or for a restricted family of graphs, does not establish the universal claim. Approximate eigenvalue calculations require rigorous bounds certifying the claimed strict reversal.

context_blocks.text: For fixed nonnegative physical edge weights \(K\), changing inverse temperature replaces \(J\) by \(\beta K\). The proposed interaction-wise inequality therefore implies that the spectral gap increases with physical temperature. Allowing zero strengths also includes the edge-addition question. The source separately asks about monotonicity of total-variation distances at fixed times; that stronger question is not part of this card’s answer criterion.

Nacu proves monotonicity in each individual coupling on a cycle. The argument also permits zero strengths by a limiting convention, including the path obtained by removing a cycle edge. This remains a graph-family result.

Kargin proves temperature monotonicity for the complete graph when all interaction strengths are equal and varied together. The theorem allows a uniform fixed external field, and hence includes zero field. Its one-parameter comparison does not establish independent edge-wise monotonicity on general graphs.

Salez’s 2023 theorem identifies the spectral gap of an order-preserving Markov chain with its optimal curvature. In that work, monotone means preservation of increasing functions of the state. It is distinct from the proposed comparison between chains with different interaction arrays.
